citation: John Carbutt, '55.—Tremont House, cor. Lake and Dearborn Streets', stereograph (Chicago: J. Carbutt, 131 Lake Street, [between 1860 and 1870]). Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-stereo-1s47905.
author: John Carbutt (1832-1905), photographer and publisher
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (LOT 12069). The left half of the card is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3688/loc_1s47905_tremont_house_left.jpg.
locator: The left half of the card: the Tremont House from across the corner of Lake and Dearborn Streets to the north-west, its Lake Street front at left nearly square to the camera, its Dearborn Street front running away to the right with the columned entrance porch and balcony; the octagonal belvedere on the roof.
rights_note: The Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph published before 1871.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-21 (T-3688) from the Library's master TIFF of the whole card (tile.loc.gov storage-services, master/pnp/stereo/1s40000/1s47000/1s47900/1s47905u.tif); the left half cropped and committed at 1400 x 1355 px, sha256 a125fadfff427aa853e714b5405d8f4d390b2208bd45f566697e25adbeea9aca. The Library's record notes the card's number as 'No. 55.'
note: The one photograph found of the Tremont House's two street fronts together: the shop fronts, the five storeys and the attic of small windows under the bracketed cornice, the Dearborn Street porch and the belvedere. Monochrome.
what_it_supplies: the Tremont House's massing, storeys and bays on Lake and Dearborn Streets
its shop fronts, porch, cornice and belvedere
